CDH / Obstetrics & Gynaecology / DISCHARGE SUMMARY
Name - Pooja Singh | 32 Y/F | UHID CDH6095305 | IP IP/26/219883
DOA - 26/05/2026 | DOD - 29/05/2026 | Consultant - Dr. Pooja Mehra, OBG Unit I

Diagnosis -
  • G3P3L3, Pre-eclampsia with severe features at 37 wks
  • Delivered by induced vaginal delivery (NVD) on 26/05/2026

Presenting complaints & history - 32/F, G3, on low-dose aspirin from 12 wks, presented with headache and BP 164/107 mmHg, urine albumin ++.

Hospital course -
  • Received Inj. Magnesium sulphate (Pritchard regimen) and oral antihypertensives. Labour induced; delivered vaginally on 26/05/2026: live baby boy, 3.09 kg, APGAR 9/10. MgSO4 continued for 24 hrs postpartum. BP settled to 137/84 mmHg on oral treatment. No fits.

Investigations -
  • Platelets 1.9 lakh/cumm | SGOT/SGPT 49/49 U/L | S. Cr 0.9 mg/dl | Urine albumin ++ | Hb 10.9 g/dl

Status at discharge - Asymptomatic. BP 134/88 mmHg, PR 78/min, SpO2 97% on RA.

ADV ON DISCHARGE -
• Tab. Labetalol 100 mg PO BD till next visit
• Tab. Paracetamol 650 mg PO SOS for fever (max 4 doses/day)
• Tab. Iron + Folic acid (IFA) 1 tab PO OD after dinner x 6/12
• Tab. Shelcal 500 mg PO BD PC x 6/12

• Stop Tab. Aspirin 75 mg (antenatal aspirin - not needed after delivery)

Instructions -
  Diet:
    • Nutritious diet + extra meal daily; GLV, milk, dal; plenty of oral fluids
    • Low salt diet - less than 5 g salt per day; avoid pickles, papad, namkeen
  Activity:
    • Adequate rest - only light household work x 6 weeks
  Others:
    • Check BP at home twice daily and maintain a chart
    • Exclusive breastfeeding for 6 months

Report immediately to Casualty in case of -
  • Severe headache / blurred vision / epigastric pain
  • Convulsions / seizures
  • BP 150/100 mmHg or higher on home check
  • Breathlessness or difficulty in breathing
  • Heavy bleeding per vaginum (soaking more than 1 pad in an hour) or passing clots
  • Baby: poor feeding / lethargy / fever / yellowish skin
  • Persistent low mood / hopelessness / insomnia / thoughts of harming self or baby

Follow up -
  • Review with BP chart - OBG OPD on 05/06/2026
  • PNC visit at 6 weeks - Obstetrics & Gynaecology OPD on 07/07/2026; bring reports: Hb, Urine routine

In case of emergency contact Casualty, Chandrapuri District Hospital (24x7).

CDH / Orthopaedics / DISCHARGE SUMMARY
Name - Thomas Gill | 79 Y/M | UHID CDH6452755 | IP IP/26/808589
DOA - 16-07-2026 | DOD - 19-07-2026 | Consultant - Dr. A. Sengupta, Ortho Unit II

Diagnosis -
  • Intertrochanteric fracture left femur
  • s/p Closed reduction and PFN fixation (17-07-2026)

Presenting complaints & history - 79/M, h/o trivial fall at home; unable to bear weight on left lower limb since then.

Hospital course -
  • Placed in skin traction pre-op. Underwent Closed reduction and internal fixation with PFN under SA on 17-07-2026. Received Inj. Cefazolin periop. Post-op check X-ray satisfactory. Distal neurovascular status intact.

Operative notes -
  • Closed reduction and internal fixation with PFN under SA (17-07-2026)

Investigations -
  • Hb 12.1 g/dl | S. Cr 0.8 mg/dl | Weight 76 kg | Post-op X-ray: fracture fixed in good alignment | RBS 107 mg/dl

Status at discharge - Afebrile, wound healthy, distal pulses felt. BP 130/76 mmHg, PR 78/min, SpO2 96% on RA.

ADV ON DISCHARGE -
• Inj. Enoxaparin (Clexane) 40 mg SC OD x 28 days (SC over abdomen)
• Tab. Paracetamol 650 mg PO TDS after food x 2 wks
• Cap. Tramadol 50 mg PO SOS for severe pain (not more than 2 doses in 24 h)
• Tab. Calcium + Vitamin D3 (Shelcal) 500 mg PO BD PC x 3/12
• Sachet Cholecalciferol (Vit D3) 60,000 IU PO once weekly x 8/52 (same day every week; with milk)
• Syp. Lactulose 15 ml PO HS x 2/52
• Tab. Rabeprazole 20 mg PO OD ½ hr before breakfast x 2 wks

Instructions -
  Diet:
    • High-protein diet (dal, eggs, milk, paneer) for healing
  Activity:
    • Walk with walker; partial (toe-touch) weight bearing on operated leg
  Wound care:
    • Keep the wound clean and dry
  Others:
    • Fall prevention - night light, remove loose rugs, use support while walking

Report immediately to Casualty in case of -
  • Pain in the calf or swelling of the leg (possible DVT - clot in leg vein)
  • Wound site redness / swelling / pus or discharge
  • Fever > 100.4 F (38 C)
  • Breathlessness or difficulty in breathing
  • Numbness, tingling, bluish colour or severe swelling of the operated leg

Follow up -
  • Removal of sutures - Orthopaedics OPD on 29-07-2026 (POD 12)
  • Check X-ray and review - Ortho OPD on 31-08-2026

In case of emergency contact Casualty, Chandrapuri District Hospital (24x7).

Dept. of General Surgery - Discharge Summary

Patient name : Manju Thakur
Age / Sex    : 57 yrs / Female
UHID         : CDH4099622      IP No: IP/26/309150
Admitted on  : 24.02.2026      Discharged on: 28.02.2026
Consultant   : Dr. Sunita Patil, MS (General Surgery) (Surgery Unit I)

Final Diagnosis:
  * Symptomatic cholelithiasis
  * s/p Laparoscopic cholecystectomy (25.02.2026)

Brief History:
  * 57/F, c/o recurrent right upper abdominal pain after fatty meals x 12 months. USG abdomen: multiple calculi in GB, largest 17 mm, CBD normal.

Course in Hospital:
  * Underwent Lap. cholecystectomy under GA on 25.02.2026. Received Inj. Cefazolin 2 g IV at induction. Intra-op: GB with multiple calculi, no spillage. Post-op uneventful; orally allowed on POD 1; drain not placed. Specimen sent for HPE.

Procedure:
  * Laparoscopic cholecystectomy under GA (25.02.2026)

Investigations:
  * Hb 12.3 g/dl; LFT: within normal limits; S. Amylase 48 U/L; HPE: awaited

Condition at Discharge: Afebrile, tolerating normal diet, port sites healthy. BP 130/70 mmHg, PR 82/min, SpO2 97% on RA.

Medications at Discharge:
- Tab. Crocin 500 mg 1-1-1 after food x 7 days
- Tab. Razo 20 mg 1-0-0 30 min before breakfast x 7 days
- Tab. Cefuroxime 500 mg 1-0-1 after food x 5 days

Advice on Discharge:
  Diet:
    * Low-fat diet - no fried / oily food, ghee, red meat
    * Soft, easily digestible diet for 1 week, then normal diet
  Activity:
    * Walk around the house several times a day
    * No heavy lifting (more than 5 kg) for 4 weeks
    * May resume desk work after 2 weeks
  Wound care:
    * Keep wound site clean and dry
    * May bathe after 48 hours; pat the wound dry with a clean cloth
    * Do not apply oil, turmeric or powder on the wound

Danger signs - report to Casualty immediately:
  * Fever above 100.4 F (38 C)
  * Redness, swelling, pus or discharge from the wound
  * Severe / increasing abdominal pain
  * Persistent vomiting / not able to take orally
  * Yellowish eyes / urine (jaundice)
  * Distension of abdomen with no passage of stool or gas

Follow-up:
  * Suture removal - General Surgery OPD on 05.03.2026 (Thu) (POD 8)

In case of emergency contact Casualty, Chandrapuri District Hospital (24x7).

Patient name : Fatima Rajput
Age / Sex    : 41 yrs / Female
UHID         : CDH5887206      IP No: IP/26/531220
Admitted on  : 10/02/2026      Discharged on: 17/02/2026
Consultant   : Dr. Farah Siddiqui, MD (Medicine) (Medicine Unit II)

Final Diagnosis:
  * Community-acquired pneumonia (right upper lobe) - CURB-65 score 2

Brief History:
  * 41/F, presented with fever with chills, productive cough with yellowish sputum and right-sided pleuritic chest pain x 4 days.

Course in Hospital:
  * Treated with Inj. Ceftriaxone 1 g IV BD and Tab. Azithromycin 500 mg OD, O2 by nasal prongs for 1 day. Afebrile for > 48 hrs; SpO2 maintained on room air.

Investigations:
  * TLC 16,200/cumm; CRP 87 mg/L; CXR: consolidation right upper lobe; S. Cr 0.6 mg/dl; Blood C/S: no growth

Condition at Discharge: Afebrile, comfortable. BP 124/78 mmHg, PR 66/min, SpO2 97% on RA. Chest: crepts reducing.

Medications at Discharge:
- Tab. Cefuroxime 500 mg 1-0-1 PC x 7 days
- Tab. Paracetamol (Crocin) 650 mg SOS for fever (not more than 4 doses in 24 h)

Advice on Discharge:
  Diet:
    * Normal diet as tolerated
    * Adequate oral fluids - 2 to 3 litres per day
  Activity:
    * Deep breathing exercises 10 times every hour while awake
    * Gradual increase in walking as tolerated
  General:
    * Influenza and pneumococcal vaccination advised
    * Stop smoking and all forms of tobacco

Danger signs - report to Casualty immediately:
  * Fever recurring, or persisting for more than 3 days after discharge
  * Breathlessness or difficulty in breathing
  * Chest pain / heaviness / sweating
  * Bluish lips / fingertips, drowsiness or confusion
  * Coughing up blood

Follow-up:
  * Review with reports - Chest OPD on 27/02/2026; bring reports: CBC
  * Repeat chest X-ray - Pulmonary Medicine (Chest) OPD on 31/03/2026

In case of emergency contact Casualty, Chandrapuri District Hospital (24x7).

Patient name : Lissy Dhillon
Age / Sex    : 52 yrs / Female
UHID         : CDH6253077      IP No: IP/26/438999
Admitted on  : 08/05/2026      Discharged on: 14/05/2026
Consultant   : Dr. Farah Siddiqui, MD (Medicine) (Medicine Unit II)

Final Diagnosis:
  * Diabetic ketoacidosis (moderate) - resolved
  * Type 2 diabetes mellitus (ketosis-prone)

Brief History:
  * 52/F, k/c/o T2DM x 6 yrs on OHA, presented with vomiting, pain abdomen and breathlessness x 1 day; precipitant: UTI.

Course in Hospital:
  * Managed in ICU with IV fluids, IV insulin infusion and potassium chloride replacement as per DKA protocol. Ketosis resolved in 34 hrs. Transitioned to s/c basal-bolus insulin; tolerating orally.

Investigations:
  * Admission ABG: pH 7.19, HCO3 12 mEq/L; Urine ketones +++; RBS at admission 526 mg/dl; HbA1c 12.0%; S. Cr 0.5 mg/dl; K 4.1 mEq/L (at discharge)

Condition at Discharge: Conscious, oriented, tolerating diet. BP 120/78 mmHg, PR 73/min, SpO2 98% on RA. Ketones negative.

Medications at Discharge:
- Inj. Insulin Glargine 12 U SC 0-0-1 at 10 PM till next review
- Inj. Insulin Aspart 4 U SC 1-1-1 0-15 min before meals till next review
- Tab. Metformin 500 mg 1-0-1 PC till review

Advice on Discharge:
  Diet:
    * DM diet: no sugar / sweets / jaggery / honey / fruit juice
    * Small frequent meals; do not skip meals
    * Adequate oral fluids - 2 to 3 litres per day
  General:
    * SMBG QID (pre-meals + bedtime) - maintain sugar chart
    * Injection technique explained: rotate sites (abdomen / thigh); keep insulin in fridge (not freezer)
    * Do not stop insulin on sick days; check sugar every 4 hours and contact hospital
    * Always carry sugar or glucose with you

Danger signs - report to Casualty immediately:
  * Hypoglycaemia - sweating / tremors / confusion: 3 tsp glucose or sugar in water immediately and report; if drowsy, nothing orally - bring to hospital
  * Blood sugar above 300 mg/dl on two readings
  * Vomiting, pain in abdomen, fast breathing or drowsiness

Follow-up:
  * Review with SMBG chart - Diabetes Clinic (Medicine OPD) on 21/05/2026

For any emergency report to the Casualty / ER of Chandrapuri District Hospital (open 24 hours).
